summary: This document is a structured research discussion report (labeled N2, negative polarity) arguing that human cognitive improvements observed after Lion's mane (Hericium erinaceus) supplementation have not been demonstrated to be NGF-mediated. It systematically reviews existing human RCTs and cell/animal studies, identifying a critical evidence gap: cognition-positive human trials do not co-measure NGF or run NGF/TrkA mediation analyses, making the popular NGF-bridge explanation an untested assumption. The document is classified as TRL-relevant for its critical appraisal of preclinical vs. clinical evidence layers.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim and Framing
content_blocks.content: The central claim (labeled NEGATIVE/assumption-kill) is that human cognitive-scale improvements after Hericium erinaceus are NOT shown to be NGF-mediated. Human MCI/AD and healthy-adult cognition trials that report scale changes omit NGF pharmacodynamic (PD) endpoints; cell/animal NGF induction data constitute a separate, lower evidence layer. The popular nootropic marketing claim — 'Lion's mane improves human cognition because it induces NGF (hericenones/erinacines → NGF → neurotrophic repair)' — is identified as an untested assumption.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch and Evidence Layers
content_blocks.content:
Two distinct evidence layers are described:
1. HUMAN COGNITION LAYER: Fruiting-body and mycelial preparations improve some human cognitive scales in MCI/mild-AD cohorts, but no NGF assay is reported in these trials.
2. CELL/ANIMAL NGF LAYER: Extracts raise NGF mRNA/protein in 1321N1 astrocytes and mouse hippocampus. Hericenones C–E specifically FAILED NGF gene induction in the 1321N1 astrocytoma system. PC12 work shows NGF-pathway potentiation in vitro.
Key confound: An erinacine-enriched mild-AD RCT tracked BDNF (not NGF) among biomarkers — substituting BDNF does not prove NGF mediation of cognition.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Key References Summary
content_blocks.content:
Four key references are cited:
1. PMID 18844328 (Mori 2009, DOI 10.1002/ptr.2634): MCI Yamabushitake RCT — HDS-R ↑ vs placebo; NO NGF endpoint measured.
2. PMID 18758067 (Mori 2008): H. erinaceus extract ↑ NGF mRNA/protein in 1321N1 astrocytes and mouse hippocampus; hericenones C–E FAILED NGF gene induction in that assay. [Cell/animal only]
3. PMID 32581767 (Li 2020, DOI 10.3389/fnagi.2020.00155, PMC7283924): Erinacine A–enriched mycelia mild-AD RCT; MMSE/IADL signals; BDNF in biomarker panel, NGF NOT listed.
4. PMID 31413233 (DOI 10.2220/biomedres.40.125): Fruiting-body RCT — MMSE ↑; authors speculate hericenones/networks; NO NGF assay.
Additional PMIDs referenced: 38004235, 40276537 (human cognition signals without NGF PD).

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations and Critical Gaps
content_blocks.content:
Three actionable limitations identified:
1. Mechanism–endpoint mismatch: Cognitive positives lack co-measured NGF; NGF positives are cell/animal only.
2. BDNF ≠ NGF: BDNF measurement in Li 2020 is not a substitute for NGF mediation analysis.
3. 'Hericenones = NGF' slogan overfits: Hericenones C–E failed NGF transcription in the Mori astrocytoma assay.

Refutation criteria: A pre-registered Lion's mane cognition-positive human trial showing plasma or CSF NGF (or TrkA pathway PD) rises with the cognitive primary AND mediation analysis attributing ≥50% of cognitive effect to NGF/TrkA change (or a pathway block abolishing cognitive benefit) would refute this claim.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis (Logical Dependency Checks)
content_blocks.content:
Three ablation conditions are specified to define what makes this claim valid:
1. Remove requirement that NGF be co-measured/mediated in same cognition-positive arm → card only restates already-LITERATURE layers (claim collapses).
2. Remove separation of cell/animal NGF from human cognitive endpoints → in vitro NGF falsely counts as human mediation (logical error).
3. Remove BDNF≠NGF marker discipline → BDNF soft-completes mediation the trial never tested (false positive).

key_findings: Human cognition-positive Lion's mane RCTs (MCI, mild-AD) do not co-measure NGF (plasma, CSF, or tissue), making the NGF-mediation hypothesis untested in humans.

Cell/animal evidence (1321N1 astrocytes, mouse hippocampus) shows H. erinaceus extract can upregulate NGF mRNA/protein, but this is a separate evidence layer from human cognitive endpoints (PMID 18758067).
Hericenones C–E specifically FAILED to induce NGF gene expression in the 1321N1 astrocytoma assay (PMID 18758067), undermining the 'hericenones = NGF' marketing claim.
The erinacine A–enriched mild-AD RCT (Li 2020, PMID 32581767) measured BDNF but NOT NGF in its biomarker panel; BDNF measurement does not substitute for NGF mediation analysis.
Mori 2009 MCI RCT (PMID 18844328) showed HDS-R improvement vs. placebo with no NGF endpoint measured.
Fruiting-body RCT (PMID 31413233) showed MMSE improvement with author speculation about hericenones/networks but no NGF assay.
No verified human trial has run NGF/TrkA pharmacodynamic measurement alongside a cognitive primary endpoint — this gap is classified as UNKNOWN.
The NGF necessity for cognitive benefit is classified as PREDICTION (untested) — no knockout or pathway-block study in humans exists.
The document is a literature-only analysis (method: lit-only); no new experimental data are generated.
Refutation threshold defined: ≥50% mediation of cognitive effect attributable to NGF/TrkA change in a pre-registered human trial, or pathway block abolishing cognitive benefit.
